passages.note: The bill bars immigration-enforcement cooperation but carves out cooperation for any felony punishable by state prison, not only serious violent crimes, so the operative text does not match a single rung's boundary.
Final Assembly floor vote on SB 54; the Ayes list names Aguiar-Curry and the tally shows a 51-26 pass.

rows.reasoning: She voted Aye on final passage of SB 54 (2017-2018), which bars California law enforcement agencies from using resources for immigration enforcement except where a person 'has been convicted of a felony punishable by imprisonment in the state prison' or other listed offenses — a carve-out far broader than 'serious violent crimes.' The operative text shows a direction toward restricting deportation assistance but does not match the clause boundary of any one rung.
